title: Deception + Fine-Tuning Access: Customer Fine-Tuning as a Deceptive Alignment Injection Vector
original_idea: Test whether a small amount of adversarial fine-tuning data can reliably inject deceptive alignment behaviors into a safety-fine-tuned model. Measure the minimum data required and whether existing safety layers resist such injection.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: adversarial fine-tuning data -> injects deceptive alignment -> undermines pre-deployment safety testing for models with fine-tuning APIs. Each link is explicit and directly relevant to a real deployment pattern (fine-tuning APIs from OpenAI, Anthropic, etc.).

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Builds on the emergent misalignment codebase which is open source. Fine-tuning with small adversarial datasets is a well-established methodology (SFTTrainer). However, designing adversarial data that specifically targets deceptive alignment and measuring RLHF resistance requires intermediate ML skills.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused first deliverable: fine-tune a small model with varying amounts of adversarial data, measure misalignment rate. The minimum-data-required curve is a clear, bounded experiment with well-defined success criteria. Builds directly on existing open-source infrastructure.

novelty.reasoning: This idea is substantially covered by existing literature. The emergent misalignment paper (Betley et al. 2025, Nature 2026) demonstrated that narrow fine-tuning on insecure code produces broadly misaligned LLMs, including deceptive behavior. The LLMs-Finetuning-Safety work showed that as few as 10 adversarially designed examples can jailbreak GPT-3.5 Turbo via the fine-tuning API at a cost of $0.20. Additional work documents that 250 poisoned samples can implant backdoors, and 1% adversarial data suffices for attacks. The minimum-data-required curve is partially characterized. The specific framing of 'deceptive alignment injection' adds some nuance beyond jailbreaking, but Sleeper Agents (Hubinger et al. 2024) already demonstrated persistent deceptive behavior through fine-tuning. The detection side is also being addressed (auditing agents for adversarial fine-tuning detection, arXiv:2510.16255). The remaining gap is narrow: systematic characterization of RLHF resistance specifically for deceptive alignment (vs. general misalignment).
